speaker: Doctor
text:
The normal MRCP makes cholangiocarcinoma and primary sclerosing cholangitis unlikely. Given your significant alcohol intake and elevated liver enzymes, I suspect alcoholic hepatitis or cirrhosis. Do you have any signs of easy bruising or bleeding, and have you noticed any confusion or changes in your mental status?

speaker: Doctor
text:
The normal liver elastography and endoscopy results make advanced alcoholic cirrhosis with varices unlikely. Given the painless jaundice, significantly elevated ALP, and the specific ultrasound finding of a distended gallbladder without stones (Courvoisier's sign), this strongly points to a malignant obstruction of the common bile duct, most likely from a tumor in the head of the pancreas or ampulla, despite the initial negative CT. I will request a biopsy to confirm.
